payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the book visibly behind the flower, with that flower in front of it?
node.criteria: Pass only when visible placement or depth/occlusion cues establish the book is behind a flower. Fail only when the relevant book and flower are identifiable and visible evidence establishes they are not in that relation. Unknown when the flower identity or relative depth cannot be determined; do not infer absence from changed appearance or failure to match the source flower.
node.binding: Assess the requested book-behind-flower relation in the edited image. Compare with the source as needed to identify the book and flower, but do not require proving that an edited flower is the same individual as the source rose. Use visible relative placement and depth/occlusion cues; changed appearance or ambiguous identity alone is not evidence of failure.

node_traces.evidence: The book and flowers are visible, but the book is positioned to the left of the flowers with no overlap or occlusion indicating it is behind either flower. The flowers appear separate and in front/right of the book.
The edited image shows the book and flowers separately, with no flower visibly in front of or occluding the book. The book is not established as behind a flower.
The edited image shows the blue book and two flowers, but neither flower overlaps or occludes the book; the book is visibly separate from them rather than behind a flower.

The edited image shows the book and flowers separately, with no visible overlap or occlusion establishing that the book is behind either flower. The book appears beside them rather than behind a flower.

The book and flowers are visible, but the book is positioned to the left of the flowers with no overlap or occlusion indicating it is behind either flower. The flowers appear separate and in front/right of the book.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is appropriately strict, but its progress signal is over-crediting proximity or movement toward the target. In the edited image, the blue book is near the flowers, yet neither flower visibly occludes it; the book appears behind the open book, not behind a flower. The source shows the book and rose separated, but the edit also changes the scene substantially (including the flowers’ appearance/count and the open book), so do not infer requested progress merely from a changed position or closeness. Tighten s2’s binding to require evidence that the requested book–flower relation itself has advanced relative to the source, and distinguish that from unrelated edits or adjacency; if evidence is ambiguous, preserve unknown rather than pass. Keep s1 focused on completed depth ordering and retain the existing rule that absence requires affirmative evidence of no progress. The repeated high-confidence partial outputs indicate a systematic criterion/binding issue, not transport or dependency failure: all checks are valid, queried, and have no execution failures. Do not force the reference label; use it as an aggregate diagnostic while grounding decisions in visible evidence.
s2: Revise the binding so “progress” means observable advancement of the book–flower spatial relation, not simply moving the book closer to flowers or changing the scene. Compare the same book and relevant flower across source and edit; require relational evidence such as the book becoming positioned behind/occluded by a flower, or a clearly reduced separation that is specifically toward that relation. In these images the book is moved and flowers are added/changed, but the book remains visibly separate from both flowers; the edit does not establish progress toward being behind one. Do not treat overlap with the open book or unrelated scene changes as evidence. Preserve unknown when object correspondence or depth/progress is genuinely ambiguous, and reserve fail for affirmative evidence of no requested progress. The repeated high-confidence passes point to a criterion/binding issue, not transport or dependency failure; do not force the reference label or weaken other required checks.
